mechanism_builds.causal_path: Inter-subject differences in baseline_RMSSD_ms, baroreflex_sensitivity_ms_per_mmHg, and LF_HF_ratio -> subject-specific conditional distribution of physiological features given segment_label -> violation of exchangeability across subjects -> conformal prediction's marginal coverage guarantee fails to hold conditionally per subject/phenotype -> coverage instability across segments from different autonomic phenotypes
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Higher inter-subject variability in autonomic measures (RMSSD, BRS, LF/HF) correlates with larger conditional coverage deviations from nominal level for segments belonging to underrepresented autonomic phenotypes
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Multi-subject dataset with at least 30 subjects spanning diverse autonomic phenotypes (e.g., athletes, heart failure patients, healthy controls)
Segments defined by standardized activity/physiological states (e.g., supine rest, paced breathing, orthostatic challenge)
Conformal prediction applied with subject-agnostic calibration set
Autonomic measures obtained from gold-standard assessments (e.g., pharmacological baroreflex testing, 24h HRV)
measurable_outcomes: Conditional coverage per subject grouped by autonomic phenotype tertiles
Coverage deviation = |conditional_coverage - nominal_coverage| per phenotype group
Spearman correlation between inter-subject CV of RMSSD and coverage deviation
Calibration curve slope per phenotype group
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Requires quantification of autonomic phenotype heterogeneity beyond simple covariates; mechanism testable via stratified conformal evaluation with known autonomic phenotypes.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Segment-dependent motion (activity_label: walking vs resting) -> increased accelerometer_variance_g2 and ECG_baseline_wander_amplitude_mV -> decreased signal_to_noise_ratio_dB and altered segment_features distribution -> covariate shift between calibration (mostly clean) and test (motion-corrupted) segments -> conformal nonconformity scores computed on shifted features misestimate uncertainty -> coverage failure in high-motion segments
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Segments with higher accelerometer_variance_g2 and lower signal_to_noise_ratio_dB exhibit larger coverage deficits (under-coverage) relative to low-motion segments
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Wearable sensor data with synchronized triaxial accelerometer and ECG/PPG
Activity labels from ground-truth video or annotated protocol (e.g., sitting, walking, running)
Segments of fixed duration (e.g., 30s) aligned to activity bouts
Conformal prediction using features sensitive to motion artifacts (e.g., HRV time-domain, morphological features)
measurable_outcomes: Conditional coverage per activity_label stratum
KL divergence between calibration and test feature distributions per activity_label
Correlation between accelerometer_variance_g2 and coverage error
Nonconformity score distribution shift (KS statistic) per activity_label
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Mechanism isolates segment-correlated artifact structure; testable by comparing coverage across activity strata with quantified artifact metrics.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Unobserved autonomic state transitions (latent_sleep_stage changes, cortisol_level_nmol_L surges) -> altered ECG_morphology_variability_index and respiration_rate_variability_bpm without change in coarse_segment_label -> violation of label sufficiency assumption -> hidden distribution shift between calibration and test segments sharing same coarse label -> conformal prediction's nonconformity scores fail to capture true uncertainty -> coverage instability
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Segments containing unobserved state transitions (e.g., NREM to REM, stress onset) show lower conditional coverage than segments with stable latent states, despite identical coarse_segment_label
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Continuous monitoring with gold-standard latent state ground truth (polysomnography for sleep, serial cortisol for stress)
Coarse segment labels that do not resolve latent states (e.g., 'sleep' vs 'wake', 'rest' vs 'activity')
Conformal prediction using only coarse labels as covariates
Physiological signals: ECG, respiration, EDA
measurable_outcomes: Conditional coverage per latent_sleep_stage within same coarse_segment_label
Coverage gap = coverage_stable_state - coverage_transition_state
Mutual information between latent state and nonconformity scores
Calibration curve deviation per latent state
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Requires ground truth latent states not used in conformal prediction; mechanism testable by comparing coverage in segments with vs without hidden transitions.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Endogenous circadian/ultradian rhythms -> predictable diurnal variations in core_body_temperature_C, melatonin_pg_mL, cortisol_nmol_L -> systematic shifts in HRV_RMSSD_ms and other signal distributions across segment_circadian_phase -> temporal non-exchangeability (morning vs night segments not exchangeable) -> conformal prediction ignoring time_of_day_hour treats them as exchangeable -> coverage varies by circadian phase
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Coverage deviates most from nominal for circadian phases underrepresented in calibration set; coverage error correlates with magnitude of diurnal variation in signal distribution (e.g., HRV_RMSSD_ms amplitude)
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Long-term monitoring >48h with precise time-stamping
Segments stratified into circadian phases (e.g., 4-hour bins: 0-4, 4-8, ...)
Conformal prediction without time-of-day covariates
Control for sleep/wake state (e.g., analyze only wake segments or only sleep segments)
measurable_outcomes: Conditional coverage per segment_circadian_phase bin
Cosinor model fit: coverage ~ mesor + amplitude*cos(2π*time/24 + phase)
Correlation between HRV_RMSSD_ms diurnal amplitude and coverage deviation amplitude
Coverage stability across days (within-phase variance)
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Mechanism distinguishes endogenous rhythms from behavioral effects; testable by time-stratified conformal evaluation with hormonal/physiological rhythm markers.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Segment-dependent annotation errors (higher annotation_error_rate_per_segment_type for difficult segments) -> systematic label noise correlated with signal features (label_noise_correlation_with_features) -> biased nonconformity score distribution (errors concentrated in specific feature regions) -> asymmetric miscalibration: under-coverage for false negative segments, over-coverage for false positive segments -> conformal prediction cannot correct because noise correlates with features
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Segments with higher annotation_error_rate_per_segment_type and stronger label_noise_correlation_with_features show larger conditional coverage deviations; direction of deviation depends on error type (false negative -> under-coverage, false positive -> over-coverage)
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Dataset with quantified annotation quality: multiple expert annotations, algorithmic pre-labels with confidence, or ground-truth subset
Segments varying in difficulty (e.g., clear sinus rhythm vs subtle arrhythmia)
Conformal prediction using noisy labels as ground truth
Annotation process metadata: expert_fatigue_index_minutes, algorithmic_prelabel_confidence
measurable_outcomes: Conditional coverage per segment_type vs annotation_error_rate_per_segment_type
Calibration curve per segment_type (reliability diagram)
Nonconformity score distribution shift between clean and noisy labels (KS test)
Asymmetry index: (under_coverage_rate - over_coverage_rate) per segment_type
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Mechanism requires known annotation error structure; testable by simulating or measuring label noise correlation with features and evaluating conformal calibration per error stratum.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Imbalanced segment representation (low segment_prevalence_ratio for rare pathological segments) -> small calibration_sample_size_per_segment for minority segments -> finite-sample variability in empirical nonconformity quantile -> conditional_coverage_per_segment deviates from nominal for rare segments while marginal_coverage remains valid -> coverage instability for clinically critical rare segments
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Conditional coverage deviation magnitude inversely proportional to calibration_sample_size_per_segment; rare segments (segment_rarity_class = 'rare') show larger absolute coverage errors than common segments
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Calibration set with known segment proportions reflecting operational prevalence (e.g., arrhythmia types: AFib 1%, VT 0.1%, normal 98.9%)
Conformal prediction with marginal coverage guarantee only
Segments defined by clinically relevant categories with varying prevalence
Sufficient test samples per segment to estimate conditional coverage reliably
measurable_outcomes: Conditional coverage per segment_rarity_class
Coverage deviation vs calibration_sample_size_per_segment (log-log slope)
Minimum calibration sample size for conditional coverage within ±2% of nominal
Marginal vs conditional coverage gap per segment
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Mechanism quantifies finite-sample conditional coverage failure; testable by sub-sampling calibration set to vary segment_prevalence_ratio and measuring conditional coverage stability.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Strong temporal autocorrelation (high lag1_autocorrelation, long autocorrelation_time_constant_s) -> adjacent segments dependent (low effective_sample_size) -> violation of exchangeability assumption -> empirical nonconformity distribution underestimates true variability -> conformal prediction intervals too narrow -> coverage below nominal; coverage instability increases with autocorrelation strength and decreases with segment_spacing_s
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Coverage decreases as lag1_autocorrelation increases; coverage approaches nominal when segment_spacing_s > 5*autocorrelation_time_constant_s; effective_sample_size predicts coverage deviation magnitude
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Physiological time series with characterized autocorrelation: HRV (autocorrelation_time_constant_s ~ 10-100s), EEG (shorter), BPV (longer)
Segments of fixed segment_length_s (e.g., 30s, 60s, 300s)
Standard conformal prediction ignoring temporal dependence
Comparison with block conformal or dependent conformal methods as benchmark
measurable_outcomes: Coverage vs lag1_autocorrelation across signal types
Coverage vs segment_spacing_s / autocorrelation_time_constant_s ratio
Effective_sample_size vs coverage deviation correlation
Interval width inflation factor needed to restore nominal coverage
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Mechanism isolates exchangeability violation due to temporal dependence; testable by varying segment spacing/length and comparing standard vs dependence-aware conformal methods.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Segment-specific SNR variations (low segment_SNR_dB due to high electrode_contact_impedance_kOhm) -> heteroscedastic prediction_error_variance (larger in low SNR segments) -> conformal prediction uses single quantile threshold (fixed conformal_interval_width) -> under-coverage in low SNR segments (interval too narrow), over-coverage in high SNR segments (interval too wide) -> segment-specific coverage instability
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Conditional coverage positively correlated with segment_SNR_dB; coverage < nominal for low SNR_bin, coverage > nominal for high SNR_bin; prediction_error_variance inversely correlated with segment_SNR_dB
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Segments with controlled SNR variation (e.g., induced by electrode gel degradation, motion, or simulated noise addition)
Ground truth SNR per segment (e.g., from clean reference signal or impedance measurements)
Conformal prediction with symmetric intervals (standard split conformal)
Prediction task: e.g., HR estimation, BP estimation, arrhythmia detection
measurable_outcomes: Conditional coverage per SNR_bin (e.g., 5dB bins)
Correlation between segment_SNR_dB and coverage error
Breusch-Pagan test for heteroscedasticity of prediction errors
Interval width vs optimal heteroscedastic interval width (oracle)
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Mechanism directly links SNR heteroscedasticity to symmetric interval failure; testable by measuring SNR per segment and evaluating conditional coverage.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Unmeasured population heterogeneity (comorbidity_indicator: heart failure, diabetes; medication_class: beta-blockers, ACE inhibitors) -> distinct latent_subgroup_membership with different signal_distribution_parameters -> segments from different subgroups non-exchangeable despite identical labels -> conformal prediction without subgroup covariates yields coverage_per_subgroup that varies unpredictably -> coverage disparities across clinically distinct but physiologically similar segments
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Coverage varies significantly across latent_subgroup_membership; subgroups with medication/comorbidity altering autonomic tone (e.g., beta-blocker users) show systematically different coverage than non-users; coverage variance across subgroups > variance within subgroups
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Population with known but unmeasured clinical heterogeneity (medication records, comorbidity codes not used as covariates)
Segments labeled identically (e.g., 'resting ECG') across subgroups
Conformal prediction using only standard covariates (age, sex, BMI)
Post-hoc subgroup identification via clustering on signal features or clinical metadata
measurable_outcomes: Conditional coverage per latent_subgroup_membership (discovered post-hoc)
ANOVA: coverage variance explained by subgroup vs residual
Subgroup detection via coverage residuals (e.g., segments with consistent under-coverage cluster clinically)
Coverage disparity magnitude between beta-blocker users vs non-users
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Mechanism requires post-hoc subgroup discovery; testable by evaluating conformal coverage across known clinical subgroups not included in prediction covariates.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Short segment_length_s -> low num_samples_per_segment and low effective_degrees_of_freedom (due to autocorrelation) -> high nonconformity_score_variance -> empirical quantile deviates substantially from population quantile -> coverage fluctuates with segment_length_s; coverage variance inversely related to effective_degrees_of_freedom
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Coverage variance across random calibration/test splits decreases as segment_length_s increases; mean coverage approaches nominal as segment_length_s increases; minimum segment_length_s for stable coverage (coverage within ±1% of nominal with 95% probability) depends on signal autocorrelation structure
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Physiological signals with varying temporal correlation: ECG (high autocorrelation), EEG (lower), accelerometer (very low)
Segments of varying lengths: 10s, 30s, 60s, 120s, 300s
Fixed calibration set size, varying only segment length
Repeated random splits to estimate coverage variance
measurable_outcomes: Coverage mean and variance vs segment_length_s
Effective_degrees_of_freedom = segment_length_s / autocorrelation_time_constant_s vs coverage variance
Minimum segment_length_s for coverage stability (within epsilon of nominal with probability 1-delta)
Nonconformity score distribution convergence rate (KS distance to asymptotic) vs segment_length_s
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Mechanism quantifies finite-sample effect of segment length; testable by sub-sampling longer recordings into varying segment lengths and measuring coverage stability.
